metadata.description: Sample FEMA flood zone polygons for Houston/Harris County, TX. Polygons are elongated along bayou corridors to reflect actual flood risk geography.
metadata.source: Sample data inspired by FEMA NFHL and Hurricane Harvey inundation maps

properties.zone_description: Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) determined. Areas subject to inundation by the 1-percent-annual-chance (100-year) flood event with detailed hydraulic analysis.
properties.name: Buffalo Bayou - Downtown / Allen Parkway
properties.notes: Historic bayou corridor running east-west through downtown Houston. Severe repetitive flood loss area. Allen Parkway and Memorial Drive flood regularly.

properties.zone_description: Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) determined. Areas subject to inundation by the 1-percent-annual-chance (100-year) flood event with detailed hydraulic analysis.
properties.name: Buffalo Bayou - Memorial / Addicks Reservoir Overflow
properties.notes: Addicks and Barker Reservoir overflow zone. During Hurricane Harvey, controlled releases from both reservoirs caused unprecedented flooding of homes that had never flooded before. Thousands of homes inundated for weeks.

properties.zone_description: No Base Flood Elevations determined. Areas subject to inundation by the 1-percent-annual-chance (100-year) flood event; no detailed hydraulic analysis performed.
properties.name: Buffalo Bayou - Energy Corridor
properties.notes: Energy Corridor business district along Buffalo Bayou west of Beltway 8. Major corporate campus flooding during Harvey. Area downstream of Barker Reservoir outflows.

properties.zone_description: Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) determined. Areas subject to inundation by the 1-percent-annual-chance (100-year) flood event with detailed hydraulic analysis.
properties.name: Brays Bayou - Meyerland / Braeswood
properties.notes: One of Houston's most repeatedly flooded neighborhoods. Meyerland has flooded in three major events in just three years (2015-2017). Many homes have been bought out by Harris County Flood Control District. Severe repetitive loss area.

properties.zone_description: Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) determined. Areas subject to inundation by the 1-percent-annual-chance (100-year) flood event with detailed hydraulic analysis.
properties.name: Brays Bayou - Texas Medical Center
properties.notes: The Texas Medical Center, the largest medical complex in the world, suffered catastrophic flooding in Tropical Storm Allison (2001). Billions in damage led to major flood protection infrastructure. Harvey (2017) caused additional flooding despite improvements.

properties.zone_description: Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) determined. Areas subject to inundation by the 1-percent-annual-chance (100-year) flood event with detailed hydraulic analysis.
properties.name: White Oak Bayou - The Heights
properties.notes: White Oak Bayou runs through the Houston Heights neighborhood and into downtown. The area has experienced chronic flooding due to urbanization and inadequate channel capacity. Project Brays-style improvements ongoing.

properties.zone_description: Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) determined. Areas subject to inundation by the 1-percent-annual-chance (100-year) flood event with detailed hydraulic analysis.
properties.name: White Oak Bayou - Garden Oaks
properties.notes: Garden Oaks neighborhood along the upper White Oak Bayou corridor. Flooding occurs when the bayou overtops its banks during heavy rainfall events. Area includes both the main channel and tributary overflow zones.

properties.zone_description: Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) determined. Areas subject to inundation by the 1-percent-annual-chance (100-year) flood event with detailed hydraulic analysis.
properties.name: Greens Bayou - Kashmere Gardens / North Houston
properties.notes: Kashmere Gardens is a historically Black neighborhood in northeast Houston with severe flood vulnerability. Greens Bayou has limited channel capacity and the area has seen chronic underinvestment in flood infrastructure. Environmental justice concerns are significant.

properties.zone_description: Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) determined. Areas subject to inundation by the 1-percent-annual-chance (100-year) flood event with detailed hydraulic analysis.
properties.name: Greens Bayou - Settegast / Trinity Gardens
properties.notes: Settegast and Trinity Gardens are predominantly minority communities along Greens Bayou with repeated flooding. These neighborhoods exemplify the intersection of flood risk and socioeconomic vulnerability in Houston. Home buyout programs have been active here.

properties.zone_description: Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) determined. Areas subject to inundation by the 1-percent-annual-chance (100-year) flood event with detailed hydraulic analysis.
properties.name: Sims Bayou - Sunnyside / South Park
properties.notes: Sunnyside and South Park are historically underserved neighborhoods along Sims Bayou in south Houston. Flooding here disproportionately impacts low-income communities of color. Harris County Flood Control has ongoing channel improvement projects.

properties.zone_description: Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) determined. Areas subject to inundation by the 1-percent-annual-chance (100-year) flood event with detailed hydraulic analysis.
properties.name: San Jacinto River - Channelview / Houston Ship Channel East
properties.notes: The San Jacinto River and Houston Ship Channel industrial corridor experienced catastrophic flooding during Harvey. Floodwaters mixed with industrial chemicals and Superfund site contaminants, creating severe environmental hazards. EPA emergency response was required.

properties.zone_description: Coastal high hazard area subject to inundation by the 1-percent-annual-chance (100-year) flood event with additional hazards due to storm-induced velocity wave action. Base Flood Elevations derived from detailed hydraulic coastal analyses.
properties.name: Galveston Bay Coastal Zone
properties.notes: Coastal flood zone along Galveston Bay subject to storm surge, wave action, and tidal flooding. Hurricane Ike (2008) produced a devastating storm surge here. The proposed Ike Dike / coastal spine barrier would protect this area. VE zones require elevated construction on pilings.

properties.zone_description: Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) determined. Areas subject to inundation by the 1-percent-annual-chance (100-year) flood event with detailed hydraulic analysis.
properties.name: Cypress Creek - Spring / Cypress
properties.notes: Cypress Creek flows through the rapidly urbanizing Spring and Cypress communities in northwest Harris County. Rapid development has increased impervious cover and runoff, worsening flooding. The Tax Day Flood (2016) and Harvey (2017) caused widespread damage here.

properties.zone_description: Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) determined. Areas subject to inundation by the 1-percent-annual-chance (100-year) flood event with detailed hydraulic analysis.
properties.name: Clear Creek - Clear Lake Area
properties.notes: Clear Creek drains southern Harris County near the NASA Johnson Space Center and Clear Lake community. Harvey caused unprecedented flooding along Clear Creek. The area is also subject to tidal influence from Galveston Bay, compounding flood risk during storm surge events.

properties.zone_description: Area of moderate flood hazard, usually depicted on FIRMs as between the limits of the 100-year and 500-year floods. Also known as Zone B or Zone X (shaded). Hurricane Harvey (2017) exceeded 500-year flood levels across much of Houston, inundating areas well outside traditional floodplains.
properties.name: Hurricane Harvey Super-Flood Extent (2017)
properties.bayou: Multiple - Buffalo, Brays, White Oak, Greens, Sims, Cypress, San Jacinto
properties.notes: Hurricane Harvey (August 25-30, 2017) dropped over 60 inches of rain on parts of Harris County over four days, making it the most significant rainfall event in US history. Over 150,000 homes were flooded, many outside any mapped floodplain. This polygon represents the approximate broader inundation extent across inner Houston, encompassing areas that had never flooded before. Total damage exceeded $125 billion. The event fundamentally changed Houston's approach to flood risk management and led to the $2.5 billion Harris County Flood Control bond (2018).
